frictions.title: Trust
frictions.definition: Whether participants feel secure enough to engage at all.

frictions.title: Risk
frictions.definition: The chance that a transaction ends in loss rather than gain.

frictions.title: Regulatory Friction
frictions.definition: Rules that fragment a market or stop it forming at all.

frictions.title: Geopolitical & Trade Volatility
frictions.definition: Sudden, systemic disruption of a specific trade corridor.

frictions.title: Macro & FX Exposure
frictions.definition: Margins eroded by currency and input-cost moves before settlement.

frictions.title: Opacity
frictions.definition: Information that is hidden, distorted, or costly to obtain.

frictions.title: Decision-Process Opacity
frictions.definition: The counterparty you can see fronts a coalition you cannot.

frictions.title: Geographic Distance
frictions.definition: How far apart counterparties are, in space or in systems.

frictions.title: Temporal Distance
frictions.definition: The gap between when one side is ready and the other is available.

frictions.title: Offering Complexity
frictions.definition: How many distinct details matter for each offering.

frictions.title: Cold Start
frictions.definition: Buyers wait for sellers, sellers wait for buyers, nobody arrives first.

frictions.title: Cognitive Bandwidth
frictions.definition: The human limit on how much choice a decision can absorb.

frictions.title: Fulfillment
frictions.definition: Getting the goods or the service delivered once the match is made.

frictions.title: Participant Fragmentation
frictions.definition: Willing traders too small, one by one, to clear the commercial threshold.

frictions.title: Technological Obsolescence
frictions.definition: An asset made obsolete before its cost is recovered.
